---
title: A complete first fit
---

This example estimates a linear conditional mean, inspects uncertainty and evaluates predictions on observations excluded from fitting. It introduces the explicit design matrices and result containers used throughout the library.

## Data and target

Let $y_i=0.5+1.4x_{i1}-0.8x_{i2}+\epsilon_i$, with mean-zero noise independent of the regressors. The slopes describe conditional associations here; a causal interpretation would require a substantive exogeneity argument.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from trex import LinearRegression

torch.set_num_threads(2)
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(600), rng.normal(size=(600, 2))])
truth = np.array([0.5, 1.4, -0.8])
y = X @ truth + (0.3 + 0.2 * np.abs(X[:, 1])) * rng.normal(size=600)
train, test = np.arange(450), np.arange(450, 600)
model = LinearRegression(device="cpu").fit(X[train], y[train], se="HC1")
pd.DataFrame({"term": ["intercept", "x1", "x2"], "truth": truth,
              "estimate": model.params["coef"].numpy(),
              "HC1 SE": model.params["se"].numpy()}).round(4)
```

Trex does **not** add an intercept to `LinearRegression`; the first column above supplies it. HC1 permits heteroskedastic errors under independent sampling. It is not cluster-robust inference for dependent panel rows.

## Predictions and diagnostics

```{python}
predicted = model.predict(X[test]).numpy()
print({"test_RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean((y[test] - predicted)**2))),
       "coefficient_covariance_shape": tuple(model.params["vcov"].shape)})
assert np.isfinite(predicted).all()
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Held-out outcomes and predicted conditional means. Noise prevents perfect outcome prediction even when the mean model is correct."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(predicted, y[test], alpha=.5, s=18)
lo, hi = min(predicted.min(), y[test].min()), max(predicted.max(), y[test].max())
ax.plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], color="black", linestyle="--")
ax.set(xlabel="Predicted mean", ylabel="Observed outcome")
plt.show()
```

## Read results explicitly

Most regression and choice models store coefficients and standard errors in `params`. GMM instead exposes `theta_` and `covariance_`; GEL uses `est` and `Sigma`; panel estimators expose `result_`. The [selection guide](choosing.qmd) and individual examples show these differences rather than implying a uniform scikit-learn interface.

Continue with [weights and fixed effects](../guides/linear-regression.qmd), [likelihoods](../guides/likelihood-glms.qmd), or [IV moments](../guides/gmm.qmd). The [API reference](../reference/LinearRegression.qmd) lists the exact options.
